page: Microsoft Azure L80as_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Lasv4 family. It features 80 vCPUs powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, with 40 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 640.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Storage is a key feature of this server, which includes 19,199 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core processing, software compilation, and encryption tasks. The server achieved a Passmark CPU score of 86,210.97 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,523.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance are also strong, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 6,074.59 GB/sec. However, single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, perform at average levels.

Given its massive local NVMe SSD capacity and high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the L80as_v4 is highly cost-efficient for data-intensive workloads that require rapid local storage access and substantial memory density. It is well-suited for large-scale database operations, software compilation pipelines, and local LLM inference tasks using small to medium models. The absence of a dedicated GPU makes it less optimal for heavy deep learning training, but its strong CPU capabilities and high-speed local storage make it an excellent fit for transactional databases, data warehousing, and high-throughput web serving.
